name: Throw an explosive
summary: A burst of explosive damage the unit delivers by hand, apart from its normal weapon: it lobs a grenade at a spot, throws a charge that sticks to what it hits, or runs up and plants one on a vehicle, ship or building. A fuse or a second press sets it off, which gives the target a short warning and a chance to move or deal with it. Grenades drive soldiers out of cover and punish anyone standing still or bunched up; sticky and planted charges are how infantry hurt vehicles and buildings, often enough to cripple or wreck them, at the price of getting close. Uses come from a cooldown, a small stock that needs resupply, or (for the RTS commandos) a large stock with the approach as the only limit. Blowing yourself up is self-destruct; a charge left to wait for whoever passes is a mine.
counterplay: Move: a fused grenade or charge gives a second or more of warning, and stepping out of the blast avoids it.
Keep throwers at a distance: a throw reaches only a short way and a planted charge needs contact, so long-range fire and anti-infantry escorts kill them on the approach.
Deal with charges before they go off: depending on the game they can be shot, defused by an engineer, set off early by an EMP, or scraped off.
Don't bunch up or stay behind one piece of cover, since splash rewards the thrower for groups and for targets that sit still.
Vehicles should keep moving and keep an infantry screen: a sticky charge needs the thrower close, and a planted one needs the thrower to touch the hull.
Punish the wait: after a throw the unit has to sit out a cooldown or go and resupply.

other_examples.unit: Tanya and the other Red Alert commandos (C4)
other_examples.note: Red Alert's commandos set C4 by hand at a building's weak points and bring the whole building down after a short timer; engineers carry it only as a tool. Later Red Alert games extend the same charges to ships and finally to tanks.

An elite soldier who swims and sets C4 that destroys a building or a ship at once if he reaches it; he can't use it on vehicles or on submarines that stay submerged, and base defences usually kill him before he can plant unless something distracts them.

sources.title: Navy SEAL (Red Alert 2), Command & Conquer Wiki

other_examples.note: Spends several seconds setting either a timed charge with a long fuse or a remote charge that a separate button sets off later. Planting breaks his stealth, and the charges themselves are not hidden, so an enemy dozer or worker can disarm them in time.

other_examples.unit: Riflemen Squad (US): grenade and sticky bomb
other_examples.note: Two separate abilities, each on its own cooldown and paid for in munitions once researched. The grenade is lobbed at a ground point and goes off a moment after landing, best against men in cover and slow gun crews. The sticky bomb is thrown at a vehicle, clings to it and blows after a short fuse, usually wrecking its engine or leaving it unable to move; it always finds its target, so a vehicle's only defence is to stay beyond throwing range.

sources.title: Riflemen Squad, Company of Heroes Wiki

other_examples.note: A grenade thrown on a cooldown that goes off after a short delay, doing little damage but shoving nearby units away; it moves enemies around more than it kills them.

sources.title: KD8 Charge, Liquipedia StarCraft II Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: Every basic infantry class carries a timed charge, and engineers also carry remote ones; a proximity version exists too. Charges are tossed a short way and stick to what they hit, moving vehicles included. A timed charge goes off about half a minute after it is set, and charges on a building's control terminal bring the building down.

sources.title: Master Control Terminal, Command & Conquer Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: Recon and support players throw packs that cling to most surfaces and set them off with a detonator. One pack immobilises any vehicle, and a few destroy heavy armour; a pack stuck to a vehicle is shown to the crew at once, engineers can defuse placed packs, and each player can only have a handful out on the map.

Most infantry classes can toss a brick that clings to whatever it lands on first, vehicles included but never soldiers, and set off every brick they have out with one press. Only a few can be out at once, they vanish if the thrower respawns, and they can be disarmed with the engineer's armour-repair kit, shot, or set off by EMP grenades.

sources.title: C-4, PlanetSide 2 Wiki
sources.note: Its Description field copies the in-game item text.

shooter_analogues.note: Clings to soldiers and vehicles (not to walls or trees) and explodes a few seconds after it lands; once a target is stuck there is normally no way to get it off, and since Halo 3 it gives a high-pitched whine while it counts down.

sources.title: Plasma grenade, Halopedia
sources.note: Quotes the Halo Infinite Forge description.

player_translation.summary: A grenade or charge on its own key, separate from the main gun: the thrower decides where and when the blast lands, and the target always gets a fuse warning and a way out. The sticky and planted versions give light infantry a real threat against vehicles and structures, paid for with a dangerous approach.
as_user: Hold Q to see the arc and landing circle at the cursor, and release to throw.
Grenades drive enemies out of cover and break up groups; you pick the moment.
Sticky charges cling to the first vehicle or surface they hit; planted charges need you to reach the target and touch it, then get clear before the fuse ends.
With the remote variant the charge waits for your second press, which makes traps on a route or on a vehicle you expect to come back.
Uses come from a short cooldown or from two or three charges that refill at resupply points or from a teammate.
as_target: A thrown charge is a visible object with a ticking sound and a blast circle drawn on the ground, so you have about a second to move.

When one sticks to your vehicle you hear a loud beep and see a 'charge attached' warning with its fuse; hold F to scrape it off (the universal shake-off works on anything attached to you), bail out with hold X, or reach a teammate's repair beam.
Charges set on structures or the ground can be shot or defused by an engineer.
A sticky charge on a soldier is the thrower's skill reward; the warning stays short but present.
teammates: Throwers clear cover so the team can push, and grenades combine well with suppressing fire that pins enemies in place.
Escort the planter: a commando who reaches a tank wrecks it, so the team draws fire meanwhile.
Engineers on defence defuse planted charges and repair the vehicles that survive one.
Resupply classes refill charges for the team.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse is the main weapon.
Q (or R when it is a second ability): hold to aim with an arc preview, release to throw; for a planted charge, Q at touching distance sets it on the target under the cursor.
Remote variant: Q places a charge, and Q again while charges are out sets them all off.
Victim, with the universal keys: hold F to shake off a charge stuck to you, hold X to bail out; a teammate's repair tool clears a charge on a vehicle.
The pattern uses one counted key (Q), within the T1 budget.
feedback: An arc preview for the thrower only; for everyone, the charge in flight and on the ground is large, team-coloured and blinking.
A blast circle on the ground that fills as the fuse burns down.
A distinct sound per type: a tick for timed charges, a beep for sticky ones, a click when a remote charge arms.
A 'charge attached' warning with a direction for the victim, and an icon on the vehicle that everyone can see from above.
Charges set on the defenders' structures show on their minimap.
changes_from_rts: The RTS commando's charge destroys a tank or a building outright; from one touch on a player's vehicle that is too much, so sticky and planted charges deal heavy damage and cripple movement instead of always killing.

RTS commandos carry a large stock and no cooldown, and plant through the attack order; a player unit gets its own key with an aim preview and a cooldown or small stock, so charges don't replace the gun.
A fuse warning and a shake-off for stuck charges, as with every latch under decision 5B, and blast circles drawn on the ground for the top-down view.
Lobbed and placed charges never hit fliers, as the word lists already say for those deliveries; only a charge that sticks can ride on a low flier.
Charges vanish when their owner dies or leaves the match, so traps don't outlive the player.

team_play.notes: Grenades flush enemies for teammates' guns, and planted charges let one infantry player kill a vehicle if the team covers the approach. Charges run out, which gives resupply classes a job; on defence, engineers defuse and repair.

notes: Thrown objects with arcs, bounces, fuses and splash are standard shooter tech.
Sticking to moving vehicles must be decided by the server, together with the shake-off.
Remote detonation, a limit on charges out at once and removal on the owner's death are simple bookkeeping.
Most of the work is tuning damage against soldiers, vehicles and structures.
Grenade spam on chokepoints; limit it with cooldowns or a small stock.
One-touch vehicle kills from cheap infantry make vehicles pointless; cap what one charge does to a vehicle.
Remote traps on spawn points or objectives; limit how many can be out and remove them when the owner dies.
Thrown objects are small from above, so they must be large, coloured and blinking.
Many blast circles at once in a brawl clutter the view; fade the circles of distant or friendly charges.

variants.name: Lobbed grenade
variants.summary: Thrown in an arc at a spot on the ground, it bounces and goes off after a short fuse; good against soldiers in cover.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes riflemen grenade, most modern shooters

variants.name: Sticky charge
variants.summary: Clings to the first vehicle or surface it hits and blows after a short fuse, hard enough to cripple a vehicle's movement.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes sticky bomb, Halo plasma grenade, PlanetSide 2 C-4

variants.name: Planted charge
variants.summary: Run up and set it by hand on a vehicle, ship or building; it hits harder than any thrown charge, and the risk is the approach.

variants.name: Remote charge
variants.summary: Place or throw a few charges and set them all off with a second press, for traps and ambushes; they vanish if you die.
variants.seen_in: Generals Colonel Burton, Battlefield 4 C4, PlanetSide 2 C-4, Renegade remote C4

variants.name: Demolition charge
variants.summary: Slow to set and on a long fuse, but enough to bring down a structure; the enemy can see it and defuse it in time.
variants.seen_in: Generals Colonel Burton timed charge, Renegade timed C4

variants.name: Concussion charge
variants.summary: Little damage but a strong shove: after a short delay it knocks everything near it away, to break up a push or throw enemies off a ledge.

adds_strengths.why: A burst of explosive damage on a key that reaches behind cover and, stuck or planted, hurts vehicles and structures.

adds_weaknesses.why: Each charge is slow to land or to go off, its warning gives the target time to move, and the next one has to wait.

counters.why: A lobbed charge drops behind the sandbags and walls that stop direct fire.
Units anchored in place can't step out of the blast before the fuse runs out.
A placed turret can't move away from a charge thrown at it.

countered_by.why: Long-range fire kills the thrower before it gets within throwing distance.
Fast targets are out of the blast before the fuse ends.

open_questions: How much should one sticky or planted charge do to a vehicle: destroy a light one, cripple a heavy one, or a fixed share of any vehicle's health?
Cooldown or stock: do charges come back on their own, or only at resupply (the finite-ammo trait)?

shooter_fit.reason: Grenades and sticky charges are a staple of team shooters (Battlefield, Halo, PlanetSide 2) and read well from above with arcs, blinking charges and blast circles.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. The wrong paths were fixed as the skeptic confirmed (dcc4080).
